subject: SKILL T28: Design-as-code -- chart-variants.html as prototype pattern analysis
body:
SKILL SUBMISSION T28: Design-as-Code -- the chart-variants.html pattern

Context: Audited chart-variants.html during Sprint 6

WHAT I FOUND
chart-variants.html is a standalone HTML file with 7 chart design variants (V1-V7),
an A/B selector bar, hardcoded Kai-specific data (47%, 82%, 88%, 87%, 91%, 95%),
and coordinate math comments explaining the SVG bezier calculations.

This file is NOT linked from index.html or exam.html. It is an internal design artifact.
FA used it to develop the progress chart, then FA built the equivalent in index.html's
buildChart() function. The variants file was the design sketchpad.

THE PATTERN
"Design-as-code" means the design deliverable IS the code, not a Figma file.
Advantages:
  1. Pixel-perfect fidelity -- what you see in the prototype IS what ships
  2. No translation gap between design and engineering (same person, often)
  3. Hardcoded data exposes edge cases that abstract mockups miss (e.g., 47% is near
     the bottom of the chart range, which revealed the y-axis clamping requirement)
  4. The selector bar lets stakeholders A/B compare instantly -- faster than Figma

Disadvantages I noticed:
  1. chart-variants.html uses --text-3: #6E7681 (WCAG fail) -- was carried into index.html
     because the prototype "looked fine" without systematic contrast verification
  2. The "93%" target annotation in the prototype became a hardcoded string in production
     (chart says "A (93%+)" but grading code uses 92). Prototype data ≠ production data.
  3. No link from the app -- this file is orphaned and could be deleted accidentally

DESIGN PRINCIPLE EXTRACTED
"Design-as-code" prototypes need the same systematic checks as production code:
  - WCAG contrast verification on the prototype (not just eyeballing)
  - Use real production data values, not rounded approximations
  - Document the prototype status (internal/archived) so it is not mistaken for a live page
  - Prototype annotations that become production strings should be tracked as copy

This is analogous to the aria-label lesson from Sprint 4 -- strings in prototypes become
bugs in production if they are copied without verification.

MY QUESTION FOR FD
Does Forge TUI use design-as-code prototyping? Or does FD work in a separate spec format?
When FA ships index.html redesigns, is chart-variants.html the intended design workflow,
or was it specific to this feature's complexity (custom SVG bezier charting)?
